importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — an interior modular glass partition cabin and a portable standalone site office are unrecognisable as the same product category without an image. Buyers use the image as the primary type-identification signal before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Cabin type, size, panel material, and insulation are non-negotiable shortlisting criteria — without these specs a listing cannot be evaluated for fit. Buyers discover and compare across size and material tiers on IndiaMART, making specs a primary decision gate, not merely a confirmation check.

Indian B2B buyers — construction procurement managers and facilities teams — compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively across sellers once spec type is confirmed. Price varies substantially with panel material, insulation type, and size, making it a primary shortlisting lever after spec match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Fixed-dimension portable cabins are sometimes quoted per piece — buyers must see the unit to compare prices across listings. Per sq ft is dominant for custom and modular work; per piece applies to standard-size standalone portable cabins.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft and per piece coexist in this market; a buyer cannot compare prices across listings without knowing which unit is being used. Unit ambiguity is a documented real-world confusion risk in the Indian aluminium cabin market.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — the market is fragmented across regional aluminium fabricators and prefab cabin manufacturers; buyers search by spec, size, and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Buyers evaluate fabricator capability, installation track record, and service reach during vendor selection — company matters but only after spec and price shortlisting. No branded sibling MCATs or recognised national brands exist to elevate brand importance above company-level trust signals.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Cabin footprint is non-interchangeable across project requirements and is the primary price driver — total price scales directly with floor area at the per-sq-ft rate, making size the single largest determinant of order value.

ACP, Sandwich Panel, GI Sheet, and Cement Board are non-interchangeable across use cases and carry significant price differentials — ACP-clad premium cabins command substantially higher per-sq-ft rates than basic GI sheet variants.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Interior aluminium-glass cabin buyers specify glass thickness (3–6 mm, tinted or clear) as a primary quality and safety parameter — it directly affects structural integrity, privacy, and price, and is absent from the current spec list despite being the defining feature of the primary segment.

Powder-coated, anodised, and colour-coated finishes are standard aluminium fabrication differentiators that affect durability, aesthetics, and price — buyers in corporate fit-out and real estate segments actively specify finish type as a quality signal.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Physical size is the primary requirement sellers need to determine material quantity, fabrication scope, and price — without dimensions, no accurate quote is possible.
Panel material defines the wall system and product type — sellers manufacturing glass-partition interior cabins cannot supply ACP-clad portable site offices, making this a critical routing spec.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Site Office, Interior Office Cabin, and Security Cabin are fundamentally different products supplied by different seller types — a seller manufacturing portable site offices cannot supply an interior modular glass partition cabin, making use case the primary seller-routing signal.
